prompt:
A line-art multi-panel storyboard of one continuous scene of a live-action short drama: one image divided into a grid of 3 columns and 3 rows of equal 9:16 panels, 8 panels read from left to right and top to bottom; cells after the last panel stay plain white. Every panel is a colouring-book drawing: contours only, in one thin uniform black line on white, most of the panel left white. Draw only the people and the few large shapes of the place (walls, doors, windows, a bed, a car). People are simple storyboard figures: hair is one smooth outline of its shape, like a cap, empty inside, with no strands, curls or waves; a face has one short line each for the eyes, brows, nose and mouth, and no stubble, wrinkles or jaw lines; a fence is its posts and top rail, a tree its outline. No texture, mesh, bricks, leaves or fabric folds; no shading, grey or solid black: dark hair, clothes and cars are outlines left white inside. Thin black panel borders, plain white gutters. Location: Garden of the wedding venue, Day, bright sunny garden light.
Image 1: the character sheet of Cassie (23), look S1
Image 2: the character sheet of Lauren (50), look S1
Image 3: the character sheet of George (55), look S1
Image 4: the character sheet of Guest 1 (25)
Image 5: the character sheet of Guest 2 (25)
Image 6: the character sheet of Natalie (25), look S1
Image 7: the character sheet of Sebastian (30), look S2
Image 8: the character sheet of Officiant (58)
Image 9: the location Garden of the wedding venue, the front view, the establishing view, facing the back wall, with no people
Image 10: the location Garden of the wedding venue, the back view, turned 180 degrees, facing the front wall, with the left wall at its right edge, with no people
Image 11: the location Garden of the wedding venue, the left-side view, facing the left wall, with the back wall at its right edge, with no people
Image 12: the location Garden of the wedding venue, the right-side view, facing the right wall, with the back wall at its left edge, with no people
Image 13: the location Garden of the wedding venue, the floor plan seen from above: its top edge is the back wall, its bottom edge the front wall behind the front view's camera, and its left and right edges the left and right walls, with no people
Image 14: the blocking reference of this segment, the same place with its people in their places at the start; use it only for where each person is and which way they face, and keep each person on that seat or spot, on the same side of the room, in every panel until a shot moves them; do not copy its colours or light
Image 15: the prop wedding-gift box; use only structure, material, and color
Image 16: the prop key; use only structure, material, and color
Draw each character so they can be told apart as in their reference image, by the shape of the hairstyle, the build and the outfit in outline only; never copy the photograph's detail. Use the character sheets only for the characters, not for their layout, white background or multiple views. Use the location images only for the layout of the space and the place of its furniture and props, drawn in outline. There is only one of each vehicle, piece of furniture and prop that the location shows, defined by the location images, throughout all panels; when a panel shows only part of one, such as a car's hood, it is that same object, and no second one appears. Each panel shows only the characters it names, and nobody appears twice in one panel.
At the start: Natalie stands at the rose-bush end of the wedding arch beside the front-row chair on the rose-bush side, holding her phone; Sebastian stands beside her under the arch on her boxwood-hedge side, hands in pockets; the Officiant stands just behind them at the centre of the arch. Lauren stands at the head of the aisle against the front-row chair on the boxwood-hedge side, her phone lowered in one hand; Cassie stands beside her on her arch side, arms folded over the empty gift box; George stands on Lauren's aisle side, holding the bouquet. Guest 1, holding up her phone, her flute on the silver tray, and Guest 2, holding a champagne flute, stand at the one small round white high cocktail table on the boxwood-hedge side.
Panel 1: Close-up insert, locked-off camera, eye-level. Cassie's hands crush the empty white gift box into a crumpled shape, its ribbon twisting.
Panel 2: Medium shot, handheld camera tracking backward ahead of Lauren down the aisle, eye-level. Lauren turns on her heel from the front-row chair and marches down the petal aisle toward the gravel path, her face rigid.
Panel 3: Wide shot, high angle from the gravel-path end of the aisle, locked-off camera. George lays the bouquet on the front-row chair on the boxwood-hedge side, and he, Cassie with the crumpled box, Guest 1 and Guest 2 hurry down the aisle after Lauren and out onto the gravel path, leaving Natalie, Sebastian and the Officiant alone under the arch.
Panel 4: Close-up insert, high angle on their hands. Sebastian places the brass house key into Natalie's open palm.
Panel 5: Medium shot, dirty single, Sebastian's shoulder at the frame edge, eye-level. Natalie, at the rose-bush end of the arch, looks from the key up to Sebastian with a puzzled frown.
Panel 6: Medium close-up, slight low angle, slow push in on Sebastian. Sebastian leans closer to Natalie with a slow, confident smile.
Panel 7: Close-up insert, locked-off camera, eye-level. Natalie's fingers close slowly around the key.
Panel 8: Medium close-up, clean single, slow push in to her face, eye-level. Natalie raises one brow and meets Sebastian's eyes with a challenging look, the key held to her chest.
Keep the characters, the number and position of every vehicle, piece of furniture and prop, and the location's spatial orientation consistent across all panels.
No text, letters, numbers, captions, speech bubbles, panel labels or watermark anywhere in the image; no photographic rendering.
